public_rationale: He forecast that 'whatever you're paying today is guaranteed to change'. In context, that means the price or what it buys. After the post, what some paid tiers buy did change. Anthropic cut Claude Code weekly allowances by about 17% from their then-current level on September 14. OpenAI cut the Pro 200 allowance for new subscribers in late September, then doubled Pro limits on October 29. But ChatGPT Plus usage was reported unchanged, and I found no post-publication evidence for Google or Microsoft. Changes at a few tiers do not establish a guarantee for whatever every user pays, and with no deadline the forecast stays open.
limitations: Relies on news reports quoting provider statements.
Did not check every vendor's pricing pages.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Because AI companies have not worked out their business models, current AI service pricing will change.

statement.excerpt: And the fact they haven’t worked out their business models means that whatever you’re paying today is guaranteed to change.

from_speaker: "they haven't worked out their business models"
"whatever you're paying today is guaranteed to change"
context: "changing the amount of value you get for $20, $100, or $200 a month"
our_interpretation: My reading is that, for AI service subscriptions generally, the price paid or what that price buys (usage allowance or plan terms) will change at some point.
'Guaranteed' plus 'whatever you're paying' makes it a universal, open-ended forecast. Changes at a few vendors or tiers show it happening, but do not establish it for all paid AI services.
No deadline is given, so stability over a finite period cannot refute it.
The causal clause ('because they haven't worked out their business models') is the stated reason. It is not scored separately.
criteria.support_condition: Dated evidence after the post that prices or included usage changed across the main paid AI services and tiers (at least OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft/GitHub consumer and business plans).
criteria.contradiction_condition: No finite record can contradict an open-ended guarantee. Long-term unchanged price and terms across major services would weaken it.
